artworks.title: Plate Number 636. "Daisy" jumping a hurdle, saddled, preparing for the leap
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence showing a horse in motion. The image features a series of still frames arranged in a grid format, capturing a horse performing a jump over a hurdle. Each frame documents a progressive stage of the horse's movement, illustrating the fluid motion of running and leaping. The background is undistracted and neutral. The sequence captures the elegance and power of the horse through its stride and airborne motion over the obstacle. The monochromatic tones lend a timeless quality to the image.

artworks.title: Plate Number 637. "Daisy" jumping a hurdle, saddled, clearing, landing and recovering
artworks.description: This is a sequence of black and white images capturing a horse jumping over a hurdle and galloping. The images are arranged in a grid format, showing the progression of the horse's movement. The background is plain with a grid-like pattern.

artworks.title: Plate Number 638. "Daisy" jumping a hurdle, saddled
artworks.description: This is a series of black and white photographs showing a horse in motion during a jump sequence. The frames depict the horse approaching, jumping over, and landing from an obstacle, capturing different stages of its movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 639. "Daisy" jumping a hurdle, saddled
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse jumping over a fence. The image is a series of black-and-white frames capturing the movement of the horse in mid-jump over the fence. Each frame depicts a moment of the stride, illustrating the horse's motion in detail. The sequence shows the progression from the approach to the landing, emphasizing the athletic grace and power of the horse. The background is simple and unobtrusive, keeping the focus on the mechanics of the jump.

artworks.title: Plate Number 640. "Daisy" jumping a hurdle, saddled
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse leaping a hurdle. The image is a sequence of black and white photographs arranged in a grid. Each row captures different stages of the jump, showcasing the motion of the horse and rider. The layout emphasizes movement without distraction. Sequential art is used to show the fluid transition from approach to landing in a horse jump. The series offers a detailed look at equine and rider dynamics, displaying the grace and power involved in the leap.

artworks.title: Plate Number 641. "Pandora" jumping a hurdle, saddled, knocking over the hurdle and landing
artworks.description: This is a series of twelve black and white frames showing a horse jumping over a fence. The frames document different stages of the horse approaching, leaping over, and landing past the fence. The images depict the graceful movement of the horse in mid-air or on the ground, showcasing fluid motion in increments. The background is a simple, dark-toned setting that highlights the dynamic movement of the horse. The series captures the study of motion, reminiscent of early photographic techniques used to analyze animal motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 642. "Pandora" jumping a hurdle, saddled; rider nude
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse jumping in a sequential motion study. The photograph shows a grid layout capturing frames of a horse and a rider jumping over a barrier. Each frame captures the horse and rider at different stages of the jump, from a canter to takeoff, clearing the jump, and landing. The series highlights changes in body posture, leg position, and movement dynamics. The progression illustrates the continuity and motion of the horse in action.

artworks.title: Plate Number 643. "Pandora" jumping a hurdle, bareback, clearing and landing; rider nude
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse jumping over an obstacle. The image shows a series of sequential frames capturing the horse's movement as it leaps and lands. Each frame depicts a different stage of the jump, showcasing the horse's dynamic motion. The photographs are organized in a grid, highlighting the progression of the movement and details such as the horse's muscles, leg positions, and posture. The background is plain to keep the focus on the horse.

artworks.title: Plate Number 644. "Pandora" jumping a hurdle, saddled, clearing, landing and knocking over the hurdle; rider
artworks.description: The series of sequential photographs depicts a man performing a jumping maneuver on a horse. The man is seen progressing from a stationary position to completing the jump over a bar. He has a mustached face, short hair, and is dressed in a light-colored outfit. The setting is outdoors with a visible jumping bar and a stable or fenced area in the background. A stepped platform is also visible alongside the jumping area.

artworks.title: Plate Number 645. "Pandora" jumping a hurdle, saddled, clearing and landing
artworks.description: The image shows a horse and rider in motion, captured in a series of sequential frames. The frames depict the horse approaching and jumping over an obstacle. The grid pattern displays the motion from a side view at the top and a rear view at the bottom. The black and white format emphasizes the contours of the horse's body and the surrounding environment, which includes a high fence or barrier.

artworks.title: Plate Number 646. "Pandora" jumping a hurdle, saddled; rider nude
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse in motion. The image is a series of black and white frames capturing the movement of a horse jumping over a fence. The sequence is split into two rows, showing different angles of the same action - a side view and a rear view.

artworks.title: Plate Number 648. "Hornet" jumping over three horses
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse jumping over other horses, captured in multiple frames. The full-sequence image is a collection of numerous black and white frames arranged in a grid. Each frame captures a different moment in the movement of a light-colored horse as it leaps over a row of dark-colored horses. The frames showcase a sequence that reveals the dynamics of the jump and the horse's body positions mid-air, landing, and preparing for another jump. This series is an early study of motion, capturing the essence of movement in static images.

artworks.title: Plate Number 649. A: "Hornet" rocking. B: "Eagle" rolling a barrel
artworks.description: This is a series of sequential images featuring a horse on a rocking platform and a horse on a wheel. The images document the movement dynamics of the horse in two different physical setups. The top row shows the horse on a platform with curved rockers, progressing from a still position to rocking motion as the horse's legs push against the surface. The bottom row displays the horse against a round, wheel-like object, demonstrating how it interacts with and moves around the wheel. The series appears to study the mechanics of movement in animals.

artworks.title: Plate Number 650. "Eagle" walking with a bucket in mouth
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a horse in motion in a sequence of twelve frames. The frames display different stages of the horse's stride as it walks in a side profile view. The background is plain and dark, contrasting with the light-colored horse. Each frame captures the positions of the horse's legs in a systematic manner, highlighting the grace and fluidity of its movement. The image is an example of motion photography, documenting animal locomotion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 651. A: Bell ringing. B: Teeter board. C: Military drill
artworks.description: This is a photograph featuring horses and one or two sheep. The image consists of black and white frames arranged in a grid format. In the first row, there are multiple photographs showing groups of horses on a platform or raised surface. The second row focuses on a white horse on a sloped plank, sometimes accompanied by a sheep. The third row shows a lineup of horses facing forward. The background includes a plain structure, possibly a fence, and trees. The sequence captures interactions and positions of the animals outdoors.

artworks.title: Plate Number 652. Horses rearing, etc.
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a sequence of black-and-white images of horses in motion. The images feature various horses in different actions such as rearing up, walking, and running. Each row captures a unique action sequence showing the horses' movement transitioning from frame to frame. The background is a solid pattern that does not divert attention from the horses. Some sequences show a horse being led on a rope, while others show two horses walking side by side. The arrangement of the images resembles a film strip and emphasizes the study of motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 653. "Buckskin" walking, lame right front foot
artworks.description: This is a series of images showing a horse walking. The photographs are arranged in two rows, each capturing a different moment in the horse's walking motion. The top row shows the horse from the side profile, walking from left to right against a gridded background. The bottom row shows similar photographs of the horse from behind, highlighting the sway of its tail and the alignment of its legs. The sequence conveys motion and is likely part of a study on animal locomotion, focusing on the horse's stride and physiology.

artworks.title: Plate Number 654. "Buckskin" walking, lame right front foot
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse in motion. The image shows a series of frames capturing the movement of a horse from both side and front perspectives. The work presents the sequences in a grid layout, showing the horse in different phases of walking. The top row of images depicts the side profile of the horse, showcasing the movements of its legs and head as it progresses across a background grid. The bottom row shows the horse moving towards the viewer. The image is in monochrome and has a structured sequence, suggesting an analytical approach to capturing motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 655. "Gazelle" walking, spavin, right hind leg
artworks.description: This is a series of photographs capturing a horse in motion. The frames show different stages of the horse's walking stride from both side and rear views. The images are likely intended for the analysis of locomotion, with the side view showcasing the horse's gait and the rear view displaying symmetry and balance. The shadow of the horse is also captured in each frame against a gridded background, adding depth to the composition.

artworks.title: Plate Number 656. "Bob" walking, free, ossification of cartilage, right front foot
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a horse in motion depicted in a sequence of frames. The image consists of multiple black and white frames arranged in a grid pattern, capturing a horse walking across a marked path. Each frame shows the different stages of the horse's gait. The top two rows display side profile views, while the bottom row presents the horse moving towards the camera. The sequential arrangement of the frames is likely part of a study on motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 657. "Lotta" rolling a box
artworks.description: This is a black-and-white image showing a horse walking and interacting with a box. The sequence consists of twelve frames capturing the horse at different stages of its movement along a platform while encountering the tilted box. The images are arranged in two rows of six, showcasing the mechanics of the horse's gait and its reaction to the box. The controlled setting suggests a scientific study of animal locomotion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 680. Oryx galloping
artworks.description: This is a photograph of an oryx in motion, captured in sequential frames. The image consists of a series of black and white photographs arranged in two rows. They depict an oryx walking or trotting across a background of a fenced area. Each frame captures a different moment in the oryx's gait, illustrating the stages of its movement. The animal's distinct long, straight horns and light-colored body are clearly depicted, as well as subtle shadows scattered around its feet, indicating its progress across a sunlit sandy surface. The surrounding fence suggests the animal is in a zoo or a similar controlled environment.

artworks.title: Plate Number 681. Virginia deer, buck, walking, startled to a gallop
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a sequence of images of a deer in motion. The image is divided into two rows, each containing smaller, black-and-white photographs. The top row shows the deer transitioning from a standing, grazing position to a full sprint in side view. The background includes a fence. The bottom row captures the deer moving away from the viewer, starting from a standing position and progressing to a sprint with dust being kicked up. The sequence is reminiscent of Eadweard Muybridge's motion studies.

artworks.title: Plate Number 682. Fallow deer, buck. A: Trotting. B: Galloping
artworks.description: This is a series of black and white frames showing a deer in motion. The frames capture different stages of the deer's movement, displaying its legs in various positions. The deer is seen with antlers and dappled markings in a controlled environment with fencing in the background. The image has a vintage quality, typical of early motion photography.
